question: Do the same ten native Cano train meshes satisfy input-exact, noise-bounded geometric replay when Poisson triangle-count variation is treated as bounded discretization rather than exact identity?
reason: M0R passed S01 and stopped at S02 solely because triangle counts were 157298 versus 157296 (2 faces; 0.001271%). Exact graph, spline, operation trace, effective parameters, axis, vertex count, both individual mesh audits, bidirectional nearest-vertex bounds, AABB and surface area all passed.

single_method_change.removed: Require primary and replay triangle counts to be exactly equal.
retained: exact graph, spline, operation trace, effective geometry parameters and axis
AABB endpoint maximum coordinate difference <=0.5 m
record OBJ hashes without requiring equality
single_method_change.threshold_basis: A round 0.01% predeclared numerical triangulation tolerance, allowing about 15 faces at the observed S02 scale while remaining 100 times stricter than the 1% surface-area tolerance. It is calibrated only on train sentinels S01/S02; observed S02 variation is 0.001271%.

execution_policy: If approved, create one new immutable run from scratch; do not reuse M0/M0R meshes, change seeds, add parents, repair meshes, retry, or inspect validation/development-test.
claim_boundary: M0R2 tests native perception-mesh materialization stability only. PASS would permit an M1 proposal; it creates no formal dataset and does not qualify collision/navigation geometry.

estimated_cost.compute: Frozen E1 CPU; twenty native mesh materializations and read-only replay comparisons; no LiDAR, simulator or training.

approval.confirmation_reference: User replied 继续 after receiving the sealed M0R failure review and the exact M0R2 single-condition proposal.
